claims.text: Adding 2–3 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles and subsequently consolidating and heat treating the alloy will produce stable Y2O3 dispersoids.
The resulting Y2O3 dispersoids will be uniformly distributed in the refractory HEA matrix.
The Y2O3 dispersoids will be coherent with the HEA matrix.
Y2O3 dispersoids will hinder dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
Y2O3 dispersoids will hinder grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature strengthening will operate through an Orowan-type mechanism.
Limiting the Y2O3 addition to 2–3 vol% will minimize the density increase.
A 2–3 vol% Y2O3 addition will avoid significant alteration of room-temperature mechanical behavior.
The proposed strengthening and creep-resistance benefits will hold at approximately 900–1100 °C under sustained loading.
The Y2O3-treated alloy will show greater than 50% improvement in high-temperature yield strength relative to the untreated baseline.
The Y2O3-treated alloy will show greater than 50% improvement in creep resistance relative to the untreated baseline.
The Y2O3-treated alloy will incur no more than a 10% reduction in room-temperature ductility relative to the untreated baseline.
The beneficial response will persist for Y2O3 additions up to approximately 3 vol%.
Y2O3 additions above approximately 3 vol% may reduce room-temperature ductility.
Y2O3 additions above approximately 3 vol% may cause unwanted density increases.
Y2O3 additions above approximately 3 vol% may cause phase instability.
